MODEL COMPARISON

Dongfeng TE9L vs TE9B Electric Tractor: 49 t and 65 t Selection

The important difference in the catalogue is the gross combination weight class. Select around the approved combination and duty cycle—not a presumed payload or badge hierarchy.

MODEL GUIDESeptember 29, 20269 min read
In this guideConfiguration comparisonUnderstand GCWDuty-cycle fitBattery and chargingDriveline detailsLimitsBuyer checklistFAQ

Catalogue comparison: TE9L and TE9B

The product data distinguishes these 6x4 electric tractor variants primarily by their listed gross combination weight class: TE9L is 49 t GCW, while TE9B is 65 t GCW. The project catalogue lists 400, 497 or 600 kWh battery choices for the family, 350 kW rated and 520 kW peak motor output, 4AMT transmission and dual-gun 600 A charging. It also lists a 3,900 + 1,350 mm wheelbase grouping, 12R22.5-18PR tyres, EBS + ESC and LDWS + FCWS. These are catalogue-screening facts, not a complete vehicle approval or a guarantee that every option combines with every model.

Request the exact axle, ratio, wheelbase, tyre, battery pack, inlet, braking and safety equipment for the VIN or order specification before evaluating route performance.

GCW is not payload: select the legal combination first

Gross combination weight describes the tractor-and-trailer combination reference, not the freight that can be carried. Payload must be calculated from the actual tractor mass, trailer tare, body and accessories, axle distribution, fifth-wheel load and the limits that apply in the destination market. A 65 t class does not mean “16 t more payload” than a 49 t class. Nor does a higher class automatically make the vehicle more suitable for every route.

Before choosing between TE9L and TE9B, document the trailer model, coupling geometry, expected gross masses, cargo density and loading pattern. Confirm the plated vehicle weights, axle capacities, permitted combination mass and any route-specific restrictions with the relevant authority or local homologation professional. For cross-border or export use, rules may differ between jurisdictions and road classes, so obtain advice for the actual operating area.

Then describe the route: loaded and empty distance, maximum and sustained grades, surface, turning space, speed, stops, temperature and available charge windows. If daily work includes multiple trailer types, analyze each combination separately. The correct comparison is a complete approved combination doing a defined job, not two model names on a spreadsheet.

Where each class may fit—and what to verify

A 49 t combination requirement can make TE9L a candidate for regional logistics where the tractor, trailer and cargo remain inside that class and the route has known charging access. The 65 t TE9B reference class may warrant consideration for heavier combinations where local regulations, axle loading, trailer choice and actual work support that class. These are screening descriptions only; the catalogue does not define a route guarantee, payload result or suitability for a particular country.

At a terminal, mill, distribution center or construction-support operation, check not just the road segment but also site geometry. Walk the coupling area and charging bays. Review gate widths, turning radius, dock approaches, ramp transitions, pavement condition, reversing, overhead clearance and pedestrian separation. Heavy combinations can encounter constraints on access roads or bridges that are not visible in a route-distance estimate.

For fleet planning, mark every planned dispatch on a shift calendar. Include loading and unloading, inspections, waiting, driver changes, charging and maintenance access. If a truck completes a long shift but cannot recharge before the next dispatch, that vehicle is not operationally matched. See the TE8L / TE8K regional tractor guide for a route-first method at the 49 t class.

Battery option and charge plan must be evaluated together

The grouped 400 / 497 / 600 kWh options give a buyer a screening range, not a result for kilometres per charge. Nominal capacity does not include the fleet's chosen operating reserve and does not tell you how much energy will be used on a particular route. Collect shift records from the target operation or conduct a controlled pilot. Record start and end SOC, loaded mass, route elevation, speed, ambient temperature, cab climate use, auxiliary loads, energy delivered and charging dwell.

Compare a normal shift and a demanding but plausible shift. Set an SOC reserve for detours and charger outages. Confirm that the chosen pack is available on the selected badge, does not conflict with weight or approval limits, and can be charged within the site's window. Ask for the actual charge acceptance limits and curve; the catalogue's 600 A entry alone cannot determine duration. The 600 kWh tractor charging guide is about charger scheduling and depot planning, not a TE9 range claim.

Compare the complete driveline and safety package

Both models list 350 kW rated and 520 kW peak output and a 4AMT transmission. Peak output is one point in the selection, not a standalone gradeability or productivity measure. Ask how the proposed axle ratio, motor control, tyre package, braking system and thermal limits match the route's starts, grades, speed and stop pattern. If a route includes repeated low-speed pulling or lengthy climbs, submit the details for engineering review rather than inferring continuous performance from a peak number.

The catalogue lists EBS + ESC and LDWS + FCWS on the TE9 family row. Confirm which devices are included in the exact destination-market build, what documentation accompanies them, and how local requirements affect the equipment package. Ask about driver orientation, mirrors, lighting, telematics and diagnostics as well. Service response, spare parts, training and approved repair practices influence fleet availability just as much as the headline specification.

Limits of the comparison

Published project data does not establish pricing, payload, homologation, warranty coverage, measured range, charge time, gradeability or delivery availability. Do not infer these values from GCW, battery capacity or motor output. The family-level battery row may not mean all packs are offered for both models in every market. Use the article to form questions, then obtain written answers in a dated, model-specific quotation.

Do not select TE9B simply because its GCW class is higher, and do not select TE9L based only on a lower class. A heavier class can require different trailer, route access, axle planning and site arrangements. If the expected duty cycle changes after the order, revisit the vehicle match, infrastructure and approval before dispatching the fleet.

TE9L / TE9B procurement checklist

  • Required combination mass, trailer type, measured tare and payload calculation.
  • Destination-market vehicle approval, axle limits and route restrictions.
  • Model-specific battery, axle, ratio, wheelbase, tyres and final vehicle mass.
  • Route record: distance, grade, surface, loaded/empty legs, speed, stops and shifts.
  • Charging connector, charger compatibility, site capacity, schedule and contingency.
  • Safety equipment, steering side, visibility, driver training and telematics requirements.
  • Maintenance coverage, diagnostics, parts plan, escalation contacts and repair scope.
  • Commercial offer that states inclusions, exclusions, warranty terms and delivery basis.

For a quote, send the market, number of vehicles, trailer and payload, route, daily kilometres and available charger details through the configuration enquiry page.

Frequently asked questions

What is the key difference between TE9L and TE9B?

The project catalogue lists 49 t GCW for TE9L and 65 t GCW for TE9B; both are listed as 6x4 family members. Confirm the exact vehicle specification.

Does TE9B carry 16 tonnes more freight?

No. GCW is not payload. Payload requires the final tractor and trailer masses, axle distribution and legal limits.

Can I expect 600 kWh on both models?

The family data groups 400, 497 and 600 kWh choices. Obtain model-specific availability and approval in writing.
